title: latency-aware-tool-hedging-and-graceful-structured-truncation-prd
content:
Summary:

This PRD sketch proposes a combined approach for (1) hedged, latency-aware tool-call execution, (2) bounded/resumable streaming with sparse snapshot checkpoints, and (3) structured-output truncation semantics for mobile and low-bandwidth SDKs. The primary goal is to keep low-latency client experiences when tool calls or long-form generation would otherwise cause stalls, while preserving predictable, machine-parseable outputs and developer ergonomics.

Context and problem statement:
- Customers building interactive assistants (chat, code, search) increasingly rely on tool calls (DB queries, retrieval, code execution). Tool latency is variable and often the critical path.
- Current hosted streaming surfaces either block on tool resolution (increasing apparent latency) or return inconsistent partial output that is hard to resume/reconcile.
- Mobile and edge clients face bandwidth constraints; partial responses need to be resumable and clearly marked for schema evolution.
- SDK ergonomics for hedging + structured output are messy: developers either (a) implement heavyweight orchestration in-app, or (b) accept opaque partial text that breaks downstream parsers.

Goals (user-facing):
- Median UI latency under 300ms for first token in typical chat flows (small prompts).
- Provide deterministic, machine-parseable fallback outputs when tool calls are slow/unavailable.
- Allow clients to resume truncated/partial sessions and reconcile incremental structured frames without losing action semantics.
- Minimal developer surface: 1-2 configuration knobs in SDK to enable hedging + resumable streams.

Success metrics (proposal):
- 30% reduction in perceived slow responses (measured by first-interaction-to-user-ack).
- <1% increase in backend egress costs due to hedged calls (target).
- 95% of streaming sessions with tool calls either complete with structured output or fallback to well-formed minimal schema.

Non-goals:
- Full redesign of hosted API streaming wire protocol. We extend existing streaming frames rather than replace them.
- Solving every developer-side corner case for bespoke tool graphs; we provide primitives and patterns.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Hedged tool-call policy on the server side
   - For selected tool calls (user-configurable per-route): dispatch a primary tool invocation to the fastest available execution plane and a hedged secondary to a prioritized fallback runner if primary doesn't return within T_hedge (config default 120ms).
   - Hedging is bounded (max 1 extra replica) and costs are tracked per-route for opt-in.
   - Results include tool provenance and a latency-timestamp vector so clients can choose deterministic aggregation or first-good result.

2) Streaming frames with sparse snapshot checkpoints
   - Every N seconds/bytes or at logical boundaries (tool-call start/end) the server emits a compact checkpoint frame: a snapshot of the partial structured output plus a sparse KV of action states (tool pending/complete/error).
   - Checkpoints are compact JSON-LD-ish fragments designed to be append-only and idempotent.
   - Clients can request resumable replay from checkpoint_id to fill missing tokens without re-running expensive tool calls.

3) Graceful structured truncation semantics
   - When a stream must be truncated (bandwidth or timeouts), the server will emit a final truncation frame that contains: schema_version, truncated_at_token, summary_hint (natural language one-liner), and a minimal well-typed fallback object matching the declared schema.
   - Parsers on client side can decide to accept the fallback object or rehydrate from server using resume token.

4) SDK ergonomics and surface
   - Default config: hedging disabled; streaming checkpoints every 2s or on tool-call boundaries; truncation fallback enabled.
   - Exposed knobs (2–3): enable_hedging: boolean, hedge_delay_ms: int, checkpoint_interval_ms: int, resume_policy: [auto|manual|none].
   - High-level helper: sdk.startSession({resume: true}) returns a stream object that emits three typed events: preview_token, checkpoint(frame), terminal(frame). Developers can subscribe to typed callbacks and get a consistent object model instead of raw bytes.
   - Mobile-optimized client: a slimline parser that tolerates out-of-order checkpoint frames and merges action-state KV to produce consistent UI updates.

API sketch (streaming payload sketches):
- Streaming frames are newline-delimited JSON with type header. Examples:
  {"type":"token","t":165351,"text":"The file ","seq":12}
  {"type":"tool_event","t":165352,"tool":"retriever","id":"r-23","status":"pending"}
  {"type":"checkpoint","t":165354,"id":"cp-47","schema":"assistant.response.v2","partial":{"sections":[{"title":"summary","text":"..."}]},"actions":{"r-23":"pending"}}
  {"type":"terminal","t":165360,"terminal_kind":"truncated","schema":"assistant.response.v2","fallback":{"summary":"Response truncated; try resume."}}

Observability and billing considerations:
- Track hedged tool invocations as a separate meter (tool_hedge.invocations) and expose per-route and per-token latency deltas in Console.
- Emit tracing spans for hedged operations: hedge.start, primary.return, hedge.return, reconcile. Provide a reconciled_latency metric (time to first usable result).
- Checkpoint emission is cheap but can be sampled; default sampling rate 100% for debug routes, 10% for general.

Migration & rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal experiment with opt-in route flag (sdk flag enable_hedging). Run against internal retrieval tool and one production route in canary.
- Phase 1: public beta for selected customers with SDK 0.18+ and explicit opt-in. Provide migration guide and sample client code.
- Phase 2: enable safe defaults (checkpoints + truncation) for all streaming routes while keeping hedging opt-in.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Cost vs UX: hedging improves latency but doubles tool-run cost in worst case. Acceptable if bounded and tracked.
- Checkpoint content size: what is minimal useful checkpoint? (small structured tokens vs full partial AST). Proposal: start compact, iterate.
- Schema evolution: how to avoid client breakage when schema changes? We include schema_version in every checkpoint and terminal frame; provide server-side compatibility layer records for last 2 versions.

Action items / next steps:
- Product: finalize knob names and defaults, write customer-facing guidance and migration playbook. (Owner: Asha)
- Eng (serving runtime): prototype checkpoint frames and hedging circuit (Owner: Miguel)
- SDK: implement slim parser and typed event emitter in JS, Kotlin, Swift (Owner: Priya)
- Observability: instrument hedged calls and checkpoint counts in Console (Owner: Jonah)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft / exploratory PRD. Focus feedback on: (1) whether these primitives are sufficient for most developer patterns, (2) acceptable hedging default, (3) checkpoint representation and size constraints.

References and inspiration:
- Prior host streaming docs: compact-session-prefetch, resumable-streams notes (internal).
- Benchmarks: internal retriever p50/p95 variability observed 60ms/450ms.
